clue.text: Good mimic could make one stare open-mouthed

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
to ape someone is to mimic them

explanation.surface: A brilliant impressionist leaves the audience gaping in wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to look with the mouth hanging open in surprise, a near synonym of staring agog.

clue.text: Leave bishop, slapped, utterly astonished

blocks.note: to go is to leave
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
smacked is a synonym of slapped

explanation.surface: Someone stunned after a bishop has been slapped, told to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: GOBSMACKED is British slang for flabbergasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gobsmacked is informal British slang for being so amazed you are speechless.

clue.text: Dior happy to wear favourite semiprecious stone

indicators.note: a happy arrangement is a fortunate new one, so the designer's name is shuffled cheerfully
something worn is surrounded by its wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
the fashion house name, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The fashion house Dior is delighted to dress its favourite model in a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of olivine, classed as a semiprecious stone.

clue.text: Typesetter in awfully poor sitcom

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a scrambled order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A typesetter has a part in a dreadful television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads as the anagram signal but it is fodder; 'awfully' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor arranges type for printing, the traditional job title of a typesetter.

clue.text: One blew on euphonium initially, then this?

definitions.text: One blew on euphonium initially, then this?

indicators.note: initially points at the starting letters of the words before it

blocks.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A musician who has played a brass instrument wonders what to try next.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a playful description of a wind instrument one might blow after the euphonium.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument played by blowing, the next thing a player might take up.

clue.text: Mourn a VIP, a remarkable Finnish runner

indicators.note: something remarkable is out of the ordinary, so the letters are not left in their ordinary order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Grieving for a celebrated athlete, a famous Finnish distance runner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' looks like part of the definition but is needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Paavo Nurmi was the Flying Finn, a distance runner who won nine Olympic golds in the 1920s.

clue.text: Potter's creation, and urn squire with kiln forged, with hint of turquoise inside

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
first letter of turquoise

explanation.surface: A potter's workshop where an urn is fired in the kiln with a touch of turquoise glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a ceramicist with urns and kilns, but it is Beatrix Potter; the T simply goes in with the other letters before they are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirrel Nutkin is the cheeky red squirrel of a Beatrix Potter children's tale.

clue.text: Girl from different habitat

indicators.note: a different version of the word has its letters in another arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A girl who has come from an unfamiliar environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword cluing.

clue.text: Telephone engineer circling number

indicators.note: circling means going all the way round, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to rig something is to engineer or fix it
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A phone repairman walking round a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person but works as the verb, meaning to manipulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them on the telephone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pastoral events turned sour, resulting in uprising

indicators.note: things that turn sour go wrong, so the letters go awry into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Country happenings went bad and led to a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is aptly rural: the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was an English rural rising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peasants' Revolt was a 1381 English rebellion, a specific historical uprising.

clue.text: Big city pub and clubs with no ale, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A big city's pubs and clubs have, astonishingly, run out of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Catalan capital and Spain's second largest city.

clue.text: Mostly elegant town

definitions.note: used attributively, as in town life, to match the adjective

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: urbane means suave and elegant

explanation.surface: A town that is largely stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means relating to a town or city, as town does when used before a noun.

clue.text: Maiden on mountain in Crete's pointing to legendary king

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
Mount Ida is the highest peak on Crete
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl on a Cretan peak indicates a mythical monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the king of Greek myth whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Head of precinct extremely upset about Irish detective

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
upset means knocked over, so in a down light the word reads the other way
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: first letter of precinct
too means excessively, extremely
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A police chief is very cross about an Irish investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely upset' reads as one phrase meaning furious; it splits into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's famous Belgian detective.

clue.text: Obama broadcast includes bit of history, every single D-Day code name

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
a bit of a word is a small part, here its first letter
includes means takes inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the president's name, letters rearranged
first letter of history
each means every single one

explanation.surface: A presidential broadcast drawing on history, naming every D-Day code word.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha Beach was the Allied code name for one of the Normandy landing sectors in June 1944.

clue.text: Wonky knees worry people from Manhattan?

indicators.note: wonky means crooked or unsteady, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Unsteady joints trouble some city dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: Manhattanites are one kind of New Yorker.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is a borough of New York City, so its residents are New Yorkers.

clue.text: Never-ending contest à la Tom and Jerry?

definitions.text: Never-ending contest à la Tom and Jerry?

blocks.note: surface reading: an endless rivalry between two competitors
setter's reading: the cartoon pair are literally a feline chasing a rodent

explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon duo are a cat and a mouse forever chasing each other, which is exactly the idiom for a drawn-out game of pursuit and evasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-and-mouse game is an idiom for prolonged toying pursuit in which neither side quite wins.

clue.text: Ambassador in West Germany in novel - author?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters appear in a new form

blocks.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
the rest of the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A diplomat posted to West Germany appears in a novel, but who wrote it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book in the surface but signals the anagram; 'in West Germany' is fodder, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist of The Old Man and the Sea, an archetypal author.

clue.text: Indicating yes, theologian at home is brought in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so these pieces sit within the drink

blocks.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
in means at home
nog is a strong ale, or eggnog

explanation.surface: A divine at home agrees when offered a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is the gesture that signals agreement, a way of indicating assent.

clue.text: With first-rate singing partner of Elton in Honolulu beach resort

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
A1 means first-rate, written with I for the one
Kiki Dee sang Don't Go Breaking My Heart with Elton John

explanation.surface: An excellent duet partner of Elton John performing at a Hawaiian resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common way of saying first-class, and the 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Waikiki is the famous beachfront district of Honolulu on Oahu, Hawaii.

clue.text: We, entertained by young socialites? They're socially inept!

indicators.note: guests entertained by hosts are taken in among them, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
debs are debutantes, young women entering society

explanation.surface: We are invited to a debutante party, and they turn out to be awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweebs is slang for awkward, unfashionable people, hence socially clumsy ones.

clue.text: Row across river in German city

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Rowing over a river in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests rowing a boat but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an old city in western Germany on the Moselle, founded by the Romans.

clue.text: Favourite aspect of carnival

blocks.note: F marks the favourite in racing odds
an air is an appearance or aspect

explanation.surface: The best-loved feature of a carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: In British racing starting prices, the favourite is marked F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a funfair with rides and stalls, close kin to a carnival.

clue.text: Black bird of prey in a hollow

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a raptor

explanation.surface: A dark raptor perched in a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a rounded depression or basin, a noun synonym for a hollow.

clue.text: Buddy (American) and I correspond

blocks.note: AM is the abbreviation for American
taken as written
things that go together match or correspond

explanation.surface: An American friend and I exchange letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests writing letters, but here it means to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Native of Lincoln checking ancestry?

indicators.note: checking means holding back, as a barrier holds what it encloses

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name
origin means ancestry or descent

explanation.surface: Someone from Lincoln researching their family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native of Lincoln' reads as a person from the English city; Lincoln is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, so a native in the strict sense.

clue.text: Appropriate to grieve over, say, a large sea creature

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: right means appropriate or fitting
to wail is to grieve loudly

explanation.surface: It is fitting to mourn a great sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The right whale is a large baleen whale, so named as the right one for whalers to hunt.

clue.text: Fail to hear young woman

blocks.note: first meaning: to not catch what was said
second meaning: an unmarried girl

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a girl who did not hear something; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to not catch a sound, and the noun is a polite title for a girl.
